## Field Notes on River Sediment

Samples were taken at four stations along the lower reach, each at a depth of two metres, over three days in spring. Fine silt dominated the slow inner bends, while coarse sand and gravel lined the faster outer banks of the channel. 1. Station A: mostly silt, with traces of organic matter. 2. Station B: medium sand, well sorted, little clay. 3. Station C: gravel bars exposed at low water.

The results suggest that deposition follows flow speed closely, as expected for a meandering lowland river.
